Synopsis:
The drow commander is a True Soul, sent to the goblin camp in order to instil some discipline in the goblins and lead their raids. She's already had one success - at the tavern - but the adventurers who infiltrated the goblin camp are her next targets. The Absolute believes they have something of value, and she must reclaim it. The players can tell her that the adventurers fled to the grove in which case she'll see the players as perfect candidates to help her infiltrate the place, having mistaken them for True Souls.

Cluster Contexts:
- GOB_DrowCommander.json: The player is standing in the goblin camp before Nightwarden Minthara, a drow True Soul who’s been sent to whip the goblins into shape and lead raids — she’s already had one success at the tavern and now wants the adventurers who infiltrated the camp found and reclaimed. Off‑screen the camp is tense from recent fights (the wolf pens combat and a freed/angry bear have unsettled the goblins) and a prisoner is being tortured for the location of a druid/tiefling sanctuary. Minthara can probe minds and forcibly mind‑meld the player to learn the grove’s whereabouts; she’s zealous, cruel, and quick to punish her subordinates (Rozzak) or extract promises from anyone she suspects is a True Soul. The player may have veiled or muddled memories—making Minthara suspicious—but if she believes the player is a True Soul she will order them to betray the grove or serve as her eyes for the coming hunt.
- GOB_DrowAndCaptured_ThreeWayDialog.json: You and your party have been brought before Nightwarden Minthara in the goblin camp, escorted by a captured goblin (Sazza) you recovered from a nearby druid grove. Minthara wields authority and can probe minds; she learns the grove’s location from the goblin and intends to raid it, demanding the player’s cooperation — either by opening the gate and signalling the assault or by refusing and fighting her. The goblin’s fate hinges on whether she (or Minthara) recognises the player as a True Soul: if she does, Minthara will spare the prisoner; if not, Minthara will execute her unless you intervene. Off‑screen events in the camp (recent fights in the wolf pens, a druid/bear presence, and other encounters with goblin leadership) help explain the tension and the stakes but aren’t spelled out in these lines.
- GOB_GoblinPriest_Branding.json: The sadistic goblin priestess is branding new converts to the cult of the Absolute. She is a True Soul - tadpoled, but unaware that is the case. She believes she is communing directly with the Absolute.

 She's one of three leaders in the goblin camp, and an important and powerful member of the Absolute's cult. She's cruel and has a sense of superiority over her own kind. Her offers of help are really a ploy to separate players from their friends so that she can imprison them and watch as the parasite eats them alive.
- GOB_GoblinPriest_Chapel.json: The goblin priestess is branding new converts to the cult of the Absolute. She is a True Soul - tadpoled, but unaware that is the case. She believes she is communing directly with the Absolute.

She's one of three leaders in the goblin camp, and an important and powerful member of the Absolute's cult. She's charismatic and friendly, in a crude sort of way, but has an underlying suspicion and curiosity. Her offers of help are really a ploy to separate players from their friends so that she can imprison them and watch as the parasite eats them alive.

context: You are standing in the goblin camp before Nightwarden Minthara, a drow True Soul sent by the Absolute to impose discipline and lead raids; she’s already asserted control once at the tavern and now wants the intruding adventurers found and whatever they stole reclaimed. Off‑screen the camp is tense from recent clashes (trouble in the wolf pens, a freed/angry bear, and other skirmishes) and a prisoner is being tortured for the location of a tiefling/druid grove Minthara intends to raze. Minthara can probe and forcibly mind‑meld people to extract or test memories, and she’s zealous, cruel, and quick to punish subordinates like Rozzak. If the player claims the adventurers fled to the grove, Minthara may mistake them for a True Soul and either order them to betray or guide the coming assault—or, if she finds their thoughts veiled or deceptive, she will grow suspicious and punish or discard them.
